extracted.intended_audience: heads of executive departments and agencies; Director of the Office of Management and Budget; federal agency legal and procurement officials
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and legal directives implementing Executive Order 13497: revocation of prior EOs concerning regulatory planning and review, and guidance to OMB and agency heads on rescinding implementing measures, effective date, and legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation subject to law and appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure actions taken to implement the order comply with existing law and that implementation is feasible only to the extent funds are available. Implementation decisions should account for statutory constraints and appropriation limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order does not create enforceable rights
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explicitly disclaims the creation of private rights or causes of action; agencies and third parties should not interpret the order as granting enforceable legal or equitable remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date — immediate
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 16. Effective Date. This order shall become effective immediately, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise specified, the order's provisions take effect upon issuance. Agencies should treat the order as immediately operative for applicable provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to contracts tied to rule promulgation
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall apply to contracts resulting from solicitations issued on or after the effective date of the rule promulgated by the Secretary pursuant to section 3(b) of this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order's effect on contracting is linked to a subsequent rulemaking by the Secretary under section 3(b); only solicitations issued on or after that rule's effective date are encompassed. Procurement officials should track the Secretary's rule promulgation to determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of specific prior executive orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1. Executive Order 13258 of February 26, 2002, and Executive Order 13422 of January 18, 2007, concerning regulatory planning and review, which amended Executive Order 12866 of September 30, 1993, are revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed prior EOs are expressly revoked. Agencies should treat those revocations as removing the authority or procedures those EOs imposed to the extent of the revocation and adjust internal practice accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind implementing measures to extent consistent with law
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 2. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the heads of executive departments and agencies shall promptly rescind any orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies implementing or enforcing Executive Order 13258 or Executive Order 13422, to the extent consistent with law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB and agency heads are directed to identify and promptly rescind subordinate instruments that implemented or enforced the revoked EOs, but only insofar as rescission is legally permissible. Legal review is required to ensure rescissions do not conflict with statute or other binding obligations.
